core_obligations: Reduce to a regular modification (proof lines 2208-2222): the parenthetical remark records that the Nagata hypothesis is only needed for the definition of rational singularity; for a modification with normal source, the dominating sequence of blowups in closed points gives a regular scheme through which the modification factors, and the comparison lemma injects the first cohomology of the modification into that of the last blowup, so it suffices to prove the vanishing for the blowup chain.

Induce along the chain (proof lines 2222-2230): applying the comparison lemma again reduces the vanishing for the last blowup to the vanishing of the first direct image of each single blowup onto the previous member of the chain; this is exactly the content of the cohomology computation for the blowup of the maximal ideal of a regular local surface, which finishes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Dominate the given modification by a sequence of blowups in closed points and reduce to the last blowup.
Use the comparison lemma to split the vanishing into the contributions of the single blowups.
Apply the cohomology computation for the blowup of a regular local surface.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a Nagata regular local ring of dimension two defines a rational singularity (statement lines 2204-2206). The proof (proof lines 2208-2230) dominates an arbitrary normal modification by a sequence of blowups in closed points, injects the first cohomology of the modification into that of the last blowup, and reduces the vanishing to the computation for a single blowup. H3: a reduction along a chain of blowups with two applications of the comparison lemma.
